exposure: Sociodemographic factors (age, ethnicity, marital status, origin, education, companion presence)
Clinical factors (parity, gestational age, labor induction, anesthesia use, childbirth position, instrumentation, perineal lacerations, episiotomy)
outcome: Profile of women experiencing vaginal birth
Characteristics of their deliveries and newborns
cohort: The study included 600 women who had vaginal births with living newborns in a public hospital in Distrito Federal between January and June 2020.
finding: The study characterized the sociodemographic and clinical profile of women having vaginal births, finding most were 20-29 years old, multiparous, delivered at term, and experienced perineal lacerations in over 50% of cases.
mod_finding: The study found that 90.17% of vaginal births were at term, 68.67% occurred in a semi-sitting position, 56.67% involved perineal lacerations, and only 3.67% involved episiotomy.
